name: Samsung Browser
statusNote: Actively developed for Android and expanded to Windows desktop releases.

windows.note: Windows desktop build published by Samsung.

android.note: Preinstalled on Galaxy devices and distributed through app stores.

availability.installMethod: App store, Galaxy Store, or direct download from Samsung.

foundation.codeLicense: Proprietary browser built on open-source Chromium

telemetry.note: No end-user telemetry posture is documented on the product pages.

trackerBlocking.note: Smart Anti-Tracking blocks cross-site tracking storage access by default.

fingerprintingProtections.note: No current fingerprinting-resistance posture is documented.

privacy.privateWindows: Secret Mode keeps browsing data out of normal history and can be locked behind biometrics.

manifestV2.note: Manifest version support is not documented.

manifestV3.note: Manifest version support is not documented.

extensions.limitations: Add-ons are distributed through Samsung's own catalogue rather than the Chrome Web Store, so desktop extension availability does not carry over.

nativeContentBlocking.note: Content-blocker add-ons and Smart Anti-Tracking are supported natively.

profiles.note: Profiles or equivalent browser identities are available.

splitView.note: Native Split View is documented in the Windows desktop build.

sidebar.note: A built-in side panel is documented.

readerMode.note: Reader mode is documented in Samsung's developer overview.

sync.note: Samsung Account sync covers bookmarks, history, and saved passwords.

translation.note: On-device translation is documented on supported Galaxy hardware.

pwa.note: An install badge, Add to Home, and standalone windows in DeX are documented.

assistant.note: Galaxy AI surfaces an assistant on supported devices.

summarization.note: Galaxy AI documents page summarisation on supported devices.

agenticActions.note: A Perplexity-powered assistant is documented acting on page, tab, and history context, initially in the US and Korea.

aiSearch.note: An ask-anything AI answer surface is documented fetching information from the web.

contentGeneration.note: Generating structured output such as travel plans from the open page is documented.

crossTabContext.note: Compiling and comparing information across open tabs is documented.

voiceMultimodal.note: Voice or image interaction is not documented for the browser itself.

dataSaver.note: Ultra Data Saving is documented only on Galaxy devices that carry the feature.

mobileExtensions.note: Add-ons are supported on Android through Samsung's catalogue.

setAsDefault.note: Can be set as the Android default browser.

offlineReading.note: Saved Pages are documented for offline reading.

addressBarPosition.note: Samsung documents placing the menu and URL bar at the top or bottom.

biometricLock.note: Secret Mode can be protected with biometrics.

backgroundMedia.note: Video Assistant includes pop-up and multi-window playback.

webPush.note: The W3C Push API has been documented since Samsung Internet 4.0.

sources.label: Samsung Browser official site
sources.note: Product scope, platform availability, and privacy feature naming.
